columns.rationale: Two-letter IATA carrier code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 across 16 rows, so every value is unique and populated (distinct_values include '9E', 'AA', 'WN', 'YV').
Full carrier name with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16, one label per carrier code (for example 'Delta Air Lines Inc.', 'Virgin America'); kept as VARCHAR since all values are free text.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 16 of UUID-shaped capture identifiers that carry no business meaning.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 1 with min equal to max ('2026-09-02T23:26:17'), a single capture timestamp rather than business data.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 1 with the only value '{}', an empty capture-tool payload.

decisions.rationale: _airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata: true and hold capture-tool values only (16 UUIDs, a single timestamp '2026-09-02T23:26:17', and the constant '{}'), so none reaches silver.
dataset.row_count is 16 and dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0, so bronze holds no exact duplicate rows and no dedupe step is proposed.

carrier has distinct_count 16 over row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so it identifies one row on its own; name is equally unique but a code is the stabler key, and a human should confirm uniqueness against the warehouse.

Both business columns landed as VARCHAR and their distinct_values are non-numeric, non-date text (carrier codes like 'B6' and names like 'SkyWest Airlines Inc.'), so no cast is justified by the samples.
carrier and name each report null_count 0 and null_rate 0.0, so both are proposed required with null_handling not_applicable.

purpose: silver_airlines is the cleaned carrier reference table derived from bronze.nyc_airlines: one row per airline, holding the two-letter carrier code and its full legal name, intended as the lookup dimension that flight-level silver and gold tables join to for human-readable carrier labels.
usage: Join on carrier to any fact table that carries an IATA carrier code; the column is unique and non-null across all 16 rows, so an inner join neither fans out nor drops rows for carriers present here. Use name only for display, since it is a free-text label whose spelling follows the source ('Endeavor Air Inc.', 'US Airways Inc.') and is not a stable key.
limitations: The table covers only the 16 carriers present in bronze (row_count 16); any flight record referencing a carrier outside this distinct_values list will not resolve and should be handled as an unmatched join on the consuming side. All three Airbyte metadata columns were dropped, so lineage back to the capture batch (extracted at '2026-09-02T23:26:17') is no longer available from this table. No dedupe was applied because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0, and no value standardization was attempted on name.
